<div class="document-sheet">

This site publishes methods, source references, synthetic examples, and reviewed result summaries. It does **not** publish real test prompts, model responses, reasoning traces, credentials, or private runtime records.

Public automation builds and tests the repository on GitHub-hosted machines. It has no connection to the local test computer or LM Studio. The dashboard is a static page, not a model endpoint.

That privacy boundary limits independent review: readers can inspect the method and public aggregates, but cannot regrade the private run from this site.

<section class="reader-section cool" aria-label="Detailed publication policy">

<details>
<summary>Maintainer policy: storage, publication checks, and result exports</summary>

## Two zones

The Git checkout is the public-source zone. It accepts source, synthetic fixtures,
configuration templates, factual reference records, and reviewed aggregate exports only.

The external state directory is the local-evidence zone. It contains permitted datasets,
raw responses/reasoning, timing, runtime inventory, settings/rollback snapshots, secrets by
reference, private audit terms, and detailed reports. It must resolve outside the checkout,
must not be symlinked into it, and is never a Pages, package, cache, or Actions input.

## Publication gate

Before the first commit and every push, release, Pages deployment, or result publication:

- reject forbidden file types, oversized files, symlink escapes, archives that cannot be
  inspected, notebooks with outputs, raw logs/data, weights, screenshots, and hidden envs;
- run the configured Gitleaks CLI plus project PII/private-path rules. CI and release setup
  installs a checksum-pinned binary; the gate blocks when the executable is unavailable;
- inspect tracked and non-ignored candidate files for filenames, file types, sizes, symlinks,
  UTF-8 content, LFS pointers, and project content rules. Archives and other uninspectable
  types are blocked rather than unpacked;
- inspect every commit reachable from `HEAD` using its raw Git object, including author and
  committer identities, the complete subject/body/trailer message, and signatures. Unsigned
  commits with the approved identity may pass; a signed commit must have a verifiable signer
  matching that approved identity or it is sent to manual review. Signed `mergetag` headers
  embedded in commits are sent to manual review because their tag provenance is not verified;
- retain the exact `Racecraft Lab Automation <info@racecraft.co>` author and committer identity
  requirement for locally or automation-created commits. A platform-created identity is not an
  exception by itself;
- accept a platform identity only from an explicitly supplied, schema-validated,
  sanitized `GITHUB_PROVENANCE_EVIDENCE` file. The offline audit never calls GitHub. The
  evidence must be a regular file that resolves outside the checkout; symlinks, in-checkout,
  oversized, malformed, duplicate, extra-key, or context-mismatched evidence blocks. Each
  exception must bind to `racecraft-lab/splash-evals`, `refs/heads/main`, actor `fgabelmannjr`,
  the exact GitHub API author and platform committer identities and valid signature, exactly one
  merged PR, matching merge and head trees (squash evidence), a successful `final gate` check
  from the `github-actions` app, and a minimal proof that the squash commit is still contained
  in the current `main` tip (`ahead` for an ancestor or `identical` for the tip, with matching
  base and merge-base SHAs). The public policy stores only the approved actor and platform
  committer contract; the collector places the exact API name/email metadata in the private
  evidence, and the offline audit matches it to the raw local commit object. Those evidence
  emails are allowlisted only while scanning that one validated commit; they are not global
  public-content exceptions, so the same address in tracked source remains blocked. The
  Actions collector may add run ID, attempt, event, and workflow-ref context; CI validates
  those fields against its current environment without storing tokens or API payloads. Missing,
  ambiguous, stale, or mismatched evidence blocks;
- inspect every tag ref/name and object type. Lightweight tags require manual review. Annotated
  tags must have an approved tagger, a `tag` header matching the reached `refs/tags/<name>`,
  a verifiable target object type, and their complete content (including body, trailers, and
  signature) is scanned. A signed annotated tag—including PGP, RFC1991, SSH, or X.509 armor—
  also requires a verifiable approved signer;
- block Git notes unless a human reviews them;
- report only redacted rule IDs and counts, never matched values;
- require an approved repo-local non-personal identity and a human/agent review of the exact
  export.

A clean tested scope is not a guarantee that arbitrary PII is impossible. GitHub still
associates activity with accounts, and outside contributors may submit personal data.
The automation identity requirement is local and exact; the platform exception proves only
sanitized API provenance for an already-merged squash commit, not ownership, capability,
security, or privacy.

Contributor and Dependabot commits do not automatically qualify for the platform exception.
The supported flow is to inspect the proposed diff, reproduce or re-author the accepted change
as a `Racecraft Lab Automation <info@racecraft.co>` commit, rerun the full gate, and then merge.
Evidence generated by Actions is private and must remain outside the checkout; locally supplied
evidence is trusted only after explicit operator review.

Changes to `.github/workflows/**`, `configs/policies.yaml`,
`src/local_evals/publication.py`, or `scripts/collect_github_provenance.py` require explicit
maintainer review. Under the current single-maintainer, zero-approval policy this is a
procedural control, not an independently enforced reviewer gate; it does not claim autonomous
tamper resistance.

## Result export

`publish prepare` constructs a fresh allowlisted export outside Git. Eligible fields include
aggregate scores, denominators, uncertainty, generic model/engine versions, public
benchmark/source IDs, protocol descriptions, limitations, and selection hashes where supplied.
It emits the stable `run_label` `local-pilot`; the raw timestamped `run_id` remains private
CLI/state bookkeeping and is omitted from the JSON payload and staged markdown. Raw prompts,
responses, thinking,
private paths, local instance/account IDs, tokens, operator activity timestamps, and
private-content hashes are excluded. Restricted prompts remain excluded even when their local
use is authorized.

The gate has two distinct export purposes. A model-capability export still requires a local
Splash measurement from the pilot suite with `held_out` exactly `true` and no contradictory
post-hoc marker. A reused pilot may be staged only when `held_out` is exactly `false` and both
`selection_status` and `calibration_heldout_separation` explicitly equal
`post_hoc_exploratory`. That second path is labeled
`post_hoc_runtime_scorer_qualification`, forces `capability_evidence` to `false`, forces the
primary objective to `blocked`, and prohibits historical comparison. It removes the
conditional-capability aggregate and any unrecognized aggregate fields. Missing, conflicting,
or partially specified classification fields block export.

A post-hoc qualification export may show that local transport completed and the scorer ran on
the reused cases. It must not be described as held-out evidence, a capability estimate, a
frontier delta, a ranking, equivalence, or improvement. The same raw-evidence exclusions and
human review requirement apply to both export purposes.

An incident blocks further publication. Revoke exposed credentials, assess Git history,
Actions artifacts/caches, Pages, releases, forks and mirrors, then use GitHub's removal
process. A later deletion does not erase earlier public copies.
